we report the complete synthesis of the lignins and humus structural phenolic monomers uniformly [13C] or [14C] labeled in the aromatic ring and the synthesis of [beta-14 C]-caffeic acid from [2- 14C]-malonate.

we have developed a complete chemical synthesis of [13C] and [14C] labeled phenolic compounds that are ubiquitous in the natural environment and involved in the transformation of xenobotics and the stabilization of atmospheric carbons.
the complete chemical synthesis and labeling of phenolic monomers is possible and that the synthesized products can be used to study the fate of phenols in the environment.

the synthesis of a variety of [13C- or 14C]-lignin and humus monomers.
a novel and efficient synthesis of [U-ring]-labeled phenolics.
the synthesis of phenolic compounds that are important in environmental chemistry and the development of a new synthetic strategy for the production of [13C/14C]-labeleld lignin and humic monomers.

all [13C]-labeledd phenolic products were synthesized and characterized with high yield.
the synthesis of [U-ring]- and [beta-C]-labeled phenolics is possible and that these products are suitable for environmental studies.
the chemical syntheses of [13C] and [14C] labeled phenols, which were used in this study, are feasible, and the yields are acceptable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a general synthetic route for the preparation of phenolic monomers, which can be used as model compounds to investigate the stabilization of phenol-derived carbons in the environment.

we have developed the first complete synthesis of all major lignin and humic structural phenols, uniformly 13C-labeled in the aromatic rings, which will enable the investigation of the fate of phenolic carbon in the environment.
all phenolic humus monomers are now available in [13C]-labled form.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to synthesize [U-ring- or side chain-13C]- and -[14C]-labele phenolic compounds, including lignin and humic monomers, starting from commercially [U-ring-]- or [U-side chain-13C- or 14C]-labled phenol.

the synthesis of uniformly [13C,14C]-labeled phenolic monomers, which are the basic building blocks of the humus and lignins, can be achieved by using commercially available [U-13C]- and/or [U-14C]-phenol.
the synthesis of [14C]- and [13C]-labeleld phenolic monomers can be accomplished in a few steps from commercially available starting material, and that the products can be obtained in good yields.
